findings.title: updateDevice SQL breaks on Postgres
findings.body: The `updateDevice` function hardcodes `?` placeholders, but Grafana supports Postgres (which uses `$1, $2, ...`). `CreateOrUpdateDevice` in the same file branches on `s.sqlStore.GetDBType()` and emits `$N` placeholders for Postgres; `updateDevice` does not. When the device limit is reached and the deployment is Postgres, this UPDATE will fail to parse and the error returned to `TagDevice`/`Authenticate` is a raw SQL syntax error rather than `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. The new device-limit feature will be effectively broken on Postgres.

findings.title: Local cache is populated before the DB call, defeating the device limit on retry
findings.body: In `tagDeviceUI`, `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` is executed before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` is called, and the entry is not removed on failure. The cache TTL is 29 minutes. With the new synchronous behavior, a device rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached` on the first request is silently allowed on any subsequent request within 29 minutes, because `tagDeviceUI` returns `nil` on a cache hit before ever consulting the DB. An attacker (or a normal user) who is denied once can simply retry and pass; after ~29 minutes the denial returns. The cache should be set only after a successful DB write, or explicitly invalidated on failure, otherwise the new `device_limit` setting is bypassable.

findings.title: Device tagging moved to synchronous, authentication now fails on device-limit error
findings.body: Previously the call to `anonDeviceService.TagDevice` ran in a goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout and any error was logged; authentication always succeeded. After this change, `TagDevice` runs synchronously on the request context, and `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned from `Authenticate`, causing the authn flow to deny anonymous authentication entirely. This is a significant behavior change that is not described in the PR description, has no docs/release-notes update, and offers no way for the caller to distinguish "limit reached" from any other auth failure. This should be an explicit, documented breaking change; consider a feature toggle or a dedicated error type that the authn layer can map to a friendly response (e.g., 429) rather than a generic auth failure.

findings.title: TOCTOU race allows exceeding the configured device limit
findings.body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` does `CountDevices(...)` and then, if below the limit, performs an unconditional INSERT. Two concurrent requests on different server instances can both observe `count < deviceLimit`, both pass the gate, and both INSERT, causing the actual device count to exceed `deviceLimit`. The PR makes no attempt to take a row-level lock, use an atomic INSERT-with-cap, or wrap the count+insert in a transaction. In multi-instance / HA deployments the limit becomes approximate and can grow without bound under load. This needs to be either documented as best-effort or enforced atomically.

findings.title: device_limit has no validation; negative values silently disable the limit
findings.body: `cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit = anonSection.Key("device_limit").MustInt64(0)` accepts any int64 from the ini file. The store treats anything `<= 0` as "no limit" (`if s.deviceLimit > 0`). A misconfiguration such as `device_limit = -1` (or a stray negative value) silently disables the feature without any error, log line, or warning. Negative values should be rejected at startup with a clear error, or at least clamped to 0 with a warning.

findings.title: Anonymous authentication now performs extra synchronous DB work per request
findings.body: When the limit is enabled, every `TagDevice` call (which is now on the auth path) runs an extra `CountDevices` SELECT against `anon_device` before the INSERT/UPDATE. The local cache (`localcache.New(29*time.Minute, 15*time.Minute)`) only mitigates repeated tags of already-known devices; new devices always incur the extra query. This adds latency to the anonymous auth hot path. Consider gating the count behind the cache as well (e.g., only check the limit when the cache misses, or only enforce the limit on first-seen devices), or otherwise documenting the performance trade-off.

findings.title: No test that an existing device can still be updated when the limit is reached
findings.body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only verifies that a NEW device ID is rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached` once the limit is hit. It never exercises the intended happy path of `updateDevice`: tagging an already-known, still-active device when the limit is reached should succeed (the device's `updated_at` should be refreshed in place). Without that test, regressions in the `WHERE device_id = ? AND updated_at BETWEEN ?` clause (e.g., the Postgres `$N` placeholder bug) would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for the authn flow when the device limit is reached
findings.body: `client.go` now propagates `ErrDeviceLimitReached` out of `Authenticate`, but no test in `impl_test.go` (or a `client_test.go`) verifies that behavior. The new feature is supposed to deny authentication when the limit is hit, yet the existing `TestIntegrationDeviceService_tag` uses `deviceLimit = 0` (via `setting.NewCfg()` defaults), so it never exercises the limit code path through the auth client. At minimum, a test that sets a small `AnonymousDeviceLimit`, attempts `Authenticate` for a new device, and asserts the returned error, is required.

findings.title: New auth.anonymous.device_limit setting is undocumented
findings.body: A new configurable option `device_limit` is added to the `[auth.anonymous]` section and exposed to the frontend via `AnonymousDeviceLimit`. No change is made to Grafana's configuration documentation (`docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/index.md` or equivalent), no sample/commented entry is added to `conf/defaults.ini`, and the PR description is empty (no "Why do we need this feature?", no linked issue, no release notes). Operators have no way to discover that the setting exists, what value to pick, what 0 means, or that it changes the semantics of anonymous authentication from "always allowed" to "denied when limit reached".
